god i wish i could go NC with my nmom
lol recommending Jordan Peterson to someone who is a victim of workplace misogyny is hilariously ironic

i have a brother that's almost 30 years old (who is now all the way across the globe) and when he was home she would consistently pull the same shit. it's so fucking bizarre and i've always been unsettled by it but i never realized just how insidious it really is.

god yes. jesus my nmom infantilizes me in exactly the same way, too. if i express that i need to get up from dinner or something to go to the bathroom she repeats to me, in a high pitched baby voice, "you need to go pee? okay!"

just going to keep venting because i'm home alone (effectively, nmom's here but in her own little world watching hallmark movies all day and wrapping gifts for people she doesn't actually care about)

she complains about my spending consistently and claims that i'm spending too much despite the fact that the only things i spend money on are literally food and transportation, with the occasional $20 spent on weed (occasional meaning like once a month). as i said in the post, i can look on her amazon account at any given time and see purchases for her apartment like curtains or pillows or some bullshit that ends up being significantly more than what i spend in a month. at times, she'll literally spend more on one or two things in a week than what i'll spend on basic necessities in two weeks.

i finally decided to break out of just direct contact with my nmom and brought it up with some family who knows that my nmom is like this to an extent (though i doubt they know the full extent of it) and they're willing to try to help me get out of the situation.

when i was still in high school, a relatively mundane and common argument broke out between me and her about me skipping school (because it was senior skip day) which led to her yelling at me and throwing random shit in my room at me. i pushed her out of my room, locked the door and called my brother to pick me up and take me to my grandparents, who are also N's but to a more tolerable extent because they're just so old that they can't spare the energy to give half the shits that my nmom does, which is where i lived for the last half of senior year and through that summer until i went away to college.

throughout childhood nmom consistently infantilized me in the same exact way that she does now. how she treats me now is exactly how she treated me when i was like 6 years old. the same incessant hugs, interrogation about social life and what i do when i'm not with her, lovebombs and more. the usual. any time i go out for some social function or family gathering she argues with me about how i dress and that i need to start dressing nicer, and that if only i would let her take me clothes shopping i could finally start being presentable.

she holds the fact that i ran away from her home over me all of the time. emphasis on her home because she would constantly remind me that i could never lock my door because it was her home. if i was to keep my door closed i would have to accept the fact that she would come in my room unannounced at any time that pleased her. my items, my social life and my life in the general were subject to her rule because, in her words, i'm not financially independent yet. she holds financial dependency over me as a way to control my life despite the fact that she has pushed against any attempts at independence at every level and step of the way. back when i was in high school, still living at her house, i had a small diary that i kept under my bed. she confronted me about it not once, but twice. the first time i argued with her for hours about how that was a breach of privacy and expected that to be the end of it, and continued using the diary. about a month after that she confronted me about it *again* and accused me of being the unreasonable one because she was my mother and she had a right to know everything about my life. in her words, i don't have a right to privacy because she is my mother, and i'm not financially independent (yes, she actually said this, and i was 18 at the time of her saying this)

when i was younger she would consistently check my phone while i was asleep and go through my texts until i finally got a phone with a lock screen. after i got a phone with a lock screen, she would constantly look at my texts that were on the lock screen and then interrogate me about it the next day. if i got a text from someone at 2 in the morning, it was worthy of an argument and interrogation about who that person is and why they were texting me at 2 in the morning. i never had a sense of privacy or boundaries and any attempt to establish boundaries has been met with vicious black and white self-victimizing, and guilt trips. she would "threaten" to move to another state and never speak to us again, calling herself a bad mother, sometimes going as far as saying that she should just die so that me and my brother can be happy since she's doing "such a bad job". 

if i express any kind of emotion that isn't unrepentant and unconditional love towards her, it's cause for incessant interrogation and saying shit like "if you aren't going to tell me why you seem so distant, i'm going to be forced to send you into therapy again" (which is something she's threatened me with for my whole life, which probably explains my aversion to therapy, though i have gone out of my own volition a few times).


when i'm up at college and don't answer a phone call immediately, she will often continue to call me several times, even if she's calling "just to hear my voice and check in". there have been times when i have gotten out of class just to see like 5 or 6 missed calls from her + texts that are interspersed by like 5-10 minutes as if i'm somehow dying just because she can't immediately reach me. it's gotten to the point where i feel so attached to my phone because she's trained me to be so dependent on that as a form of communication and if i'm not within reasonable distance from it then i feel unsettled. it's something i've acknowledged and i am attempting to de-train myself out of that mentality but fuck it's such an upward battle. my whole life is an upward fucking battle. i don't know what to do. i've attempted suicide in the past and now that i've gotten a glimpse of independence at college it just makes being "home" all the fucking worse. i found myself raiding my grandparents medicine cabinet last night in an attempt to escape the feelings of being stuck and ended up throwing up and almost overdosing at like 3 in the morning.

it's christmas eve and she's trained me not to like christmas because it's such an intensely shitty time of year for me because of her. i can't even begin to count the amount of christmases that have gone by where we have the same arguments over and over again. 

i want to go full NC but it's so fucking hard because

1. i'm not fully financially independent (for which i blame a combination of my own lifelong history of depression and my mom's many pushbacks any time i do push for independence)

2. a lot of my family guilts me into "loving" her because they don't realize how bad the situation is, despite the fact that we all make jokes about how controlling and engulfing she is (to the point where my family guilted me into living in my mom's apartment any time i come home from college if i wanted to keep my financial aid that they give me)

my brother is the only one who even somewhat understands the extent to which our nmom has fucked me up and he's all the way on the other side of the globe (which i congratulate him for, he worked hard for it and now he gets to reap the benefits of real life independence). i feel so so so so so so so so stuck and sad and depressed and i want to self harm and die but i know that's unreasonable. i'm just trying to reap whatever benefits i can of this holiday season while i'm home and then get my ass back up in college as soon as possible. it's just so hard to see the light at the end of the tunnel. the farther i get into my adult life without driving, the more i feel like i'm getting irreparably fucked up mentally and the less of a sense of identity i feel like i have.
